answer.evidence: The main body is a flat elliptical opening in the ice. The width profile runs 9, 12, 13, 14, 13, 10, 5 across rows 6-14, and dark water fills rows 8-12 inside a pale ice rim. Below the opening there is only a 2-row blue ice lip (rows 13-14) with no real vertical front face of 3 or more rows. The thin rod at the top (rows 2-9, width 2) is decor. The hole is a ground-level feature, so it reads as a flat top-down shape with at most a 2-row front.

That is fewer than 3 rows, so no real vertical south face is drawn. The rod and line above (rows 2-10) are decor. The object is essentially a flat hole in the ice with a very thin front lip.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small ground-level prop under one tile, so the per-tile facts read 0 and I judged it by eye. Its 12 distinct colours are on par with the bench (14), hedge (11) and lamp (14) references. It shows about 5 steps: a bright ice-rim highlight, light and mid icy blues, dark water and a deep edge. The dark edge pixels are 0% near-neutral, so the outline is tinted dark blue, not black, and it matches the adjacent ice and water. There are no flat 5x5 blocks (0% near-flat). The rim breaks up into chips and the water has a glint. It is simpler than the stall or well, but a hole in the ice is inherently a simple shape, and it is no thinner or more sticker-like than the bench. A careful artist would accept it beside the small references, though the surface texture is modest.
